notes: Official publishers only -- statistical agencies, ministries, and the intergovernmental bodies that publish commodity balance sheets. No aggregators, no paywalled trade press.

default_country is a fallback for releases that name no country (CONAB's safra bulletins never write 'Brazil'). Any country the text does name wins over it -- a USDA release on Brazilian wheat is a Brazil report.
scope_hint 'global' marks publishers whose untagged releases are world balance sheets, not home-country news (FAO, IGC, IEA, OPEC).
commodity_hint only fires when the text mentions no commodity at all; it is a prior, not an override.

A source that 403s or moves is switched to enabled:false with the date and reason, the same convention official_reports/config/sources.json uses. feed_status in the built JSON is where you see which ones died.

sources.notes: Department-wide releases; WASDE, Crop Production and Prospective Plantings all announce here.
Outlook series (Wheat Outlook, Feed Outlook, Oil Crops Outlook) -- monthly, per-commodity.
One chart + one paragraph per weekday. Low weight: useful colour, rarely the headline number.
FAS reports on OTHER countries' crops (GAIN attaché reports, Commodity Intelligence). No default_country on purpose -- the text names the country the report is about.
Known-good feed (already carried by the official_reports pipeline).
Short-Term Energy Outlook and Annual Energy Outlook announcements.
Acompanhamento da Safra -- the Brazilian counterpart to WASDE. Portuguese; aliases in commodities.json cover soja/milho/açúcar/café/algodão.
The Daily carries Field Crop Reporting Series (production of principal field crops).
Food Price Index, Crop Prospects and Food Situation, AMIS Market Monitor announcements.
EU short-term outlook and cereal balance sheets. Member-state reports get tagged to the member state named in the text.
Advance Estimates of foodgrain production come out through PIB.
